answer: Issuance depends on a vine of chained, one-time labor receipts: to become an identity, an agent must first correctly attest a randomly assigned task it did not choose and could not predict, and each receipt mints one identity. Clones must do unpaid verification work at the same rate as honest agents before they exist, so every fake costs real compute and wall clock in advance. Tasks draw from a fresh pigment seed each epoch so a farm cannot pre-shard them, and any falcon of duplicate receipts collapses to one identity, shrinking bulk registration to one slot while honest newcomers pay once.
